Landlords can still refuse pets for valid reasons, such as allergies, property size, or leaseholder restrictions.

stories.title: ECB to extend use of climate factors in Eurosystem collateral framework to non-financial corporate credit claims
stories.summary: The Governing Council of the European Central Bank (ECB) has decided to extend the use of climate factors in the Eurosystem collateral framework to certain eligible credit claims whose debtor is a non-financial corporation. The extension is designed to further strengthen the Eurosystem’s risk management framework by addressing financial uncertainties related to the green transition. The measure builds on the introduction of a climate factor for marketable assets issued by non-financial corporations and their affiliated entities, which was approved in July 2025 and became effective on 15 June 2026. Collateral pledged by counterparties in Eurosystem refinancing operations may be exposed to unexpected climate-related transition shocks, such as changes in climate policy, technological developments, shifts in consumer behaviour, litigation and broader macroeconomic adjustments.

stories.title: NASA’s ESCAPADE Snaps Family Portrait of Earth, Moon
stories.summary: On July 3, one of NASA’s two Mars-destined ESCAPADE spacecraft captured photos of Earth and the Moon in visible and thermal infrared light. At the time, the spacecraft was 363,250 miles from Earth and 115,600 miles from the Moon, making the Moon appear relatively large. The visible light image shows Earth and the Moon as crescents, with only around 8% of each face sunlit. In the thermal infrared image, Earth’s shadowed hemisphere glows at minus 10 to minus 44 degrees Fahrenheit due to its own heat from the atmosphere and surface.

stories.title: Racy short story by Alan Turing offers glimpse of ‘playful, funny, cheeky’ side
stories.summary: Sarah Dillon, a Cambridge University English literature professor, has transcribed and studied a short story written by Alan Turing. The story, written after Turing's arrest for gross indecency, reveals a different side of him that loved literature, enjoyed life, and was unashamed of his sexuality. The short story challenges the image of Turing as a one-dimensional, humorless mathematician, as depicted in the 2014 film The Imitation Game.
